items.title: How Much Does a 62-Year-Old Need Invested to Collect $7,950 a Month for Life?
items.summary: The capital requirement to generate nearly $8,000 a month for life swings by more than $1.7 million depending on the yield strategy a 62-year-old chooses, and the cheaper-looking option often destroys the retirement it was supposed to fund.

items.title: In the Age of AI, Cash Is Still King
items.summary: Savings accounts, short-term Treasury bills and money-market funds paid little yield when interest rates were near zero.  The Federal Reserve’s rate hikes starting in 2022 reset the bar for what cash could pay out to investors.  On top of that, the advance of technology and new forms of banking and money not only add new competitors for cash—neobanks, stablecoins, tokenized or exchange-traded Treasury bills—but make it increasingly easy to switch cash from where it earns little, to where it earns more.

items.title: ‘Consumer Inertia’ Is in Meta Muse’s Crosshairs. These Stocks Are Getting Hammered.
items.summary: Shares of AT&T, insurers, travel agents and other consumer stocks have been hit by worries that Muse will hurt their businesses.

items.title: Meta’s Muse AI Agent Triggers Worries About Brokerage Stocks
items.summary: Concerns about AI have repeatedly sparked selloffs of shares of brokerage firms. On Tuesday, Meta’s Muse AI agent became the latest catalyst.

items.title: How Meta's Muse, Vanguard AI Threat Triggered Schwab Sell Signal
items.summary: Charles Schwab stock recovered only modestly on Wednesday morning, a day after leading a wide swath of brokerage, bank and other financial stocks lower as AI-fueled competition heats up.  Rapid adoption of Meta Platforms' Muse personal AI agent and a growing threat from Altruist, an AI platform for financial advisors that was recently acquired by Vanguard, have highlighted two very different type of risks to Schwab's business.

items.title: How Does Meta's Muse AI Raise Risks for Banks & Other Finance Firms?
items.summary: Meta's Muse AI raises risks for finance firms by making it easier for customers to compare rates, fees and products, and move deposits or assets.
